item.title: A 12,900-year-old cave in Türkiye reveals a forgotten world of hunter-gatherers and ancient fires
item.description: The Koskarlı Cave in Türkiye has unveiled a remarkable 12,900-year-old layer showcasing the life of hunter-gatherers. This extraordinary find includes evidence of Epipalaeolithic individuals, featuring items like a hearth, stone tools, and personal ornaments. Importantly, these discoveries hint at cultural links between regions such as Anatolia, the Caucasus, and the Levant, paving the way for deeper insights into prehistoric societies.

item.title: Total solar eclipse 2026: Here’s where Americans will see today’s eclipse
item.description: Today brings a spectacular total solar eclipse as the Moon neatly aligns between Earth and the Sun. This extraordinary event will unveil its shadow over the Northern Hemisphere, with totality observable in regions like Greenland, Iceland, and certain areas of Spain and Portugal. A partial eclipse will also captivate viewers in various European countries and parts of North America.

item.title: Colorado cleaned up Rocky Mountain Arsenal; refuge now supports more than 330 animal species
item.description: The Rocky Mountain Arsenal National Wildlife Refuge in Colorado has undergone a remarkable transformation from a heavily contaminated chemical weapons and pesticide production site into a thriving wildlife sanctuary. This story explores the Arsenal’s polluted industrial past, decades-long cleanup and ongoing environmental monitoring, while highlighting the return of bison, bald eagles, black-footed ferrets and hundreds of other species.

item.title: Lake Erie fish gather near low-oxygen zones as climate change reshapes habitat
item.description: Fish in Lake Erie appear to gather near low-oxygen areas instead of steering clear of them, which reshapes the landscape of their habitat. This unexpected behavior not only changes how fish interact but also contradicts prior theories about their avoidance strategies. With climate change potentially worsening these hypoxic conditions, understanding these dynamics becomes vital for sustainable fisheries management and ecological monitoring.

item.title: A 1,300-year-old Byzantine shipwreck yielded 600g of gold, hinting at an imperial passenger on board
item.description: A shipwreck discovered off Croatia's Mljet island yielded a significant gold treasure. This find includes a gold signet ring and a gem-encrusted belt, dating back centuries. The vessel's cargo offers new insights into the Byzantine Empire's trade and history. Researchers are analyzing artifacts to understand the voyage's purpose and context. This discovery challenges previous notions about the region during the early medieval period.

item.title: Meet Rosie, 5, who turned a princess scooter ride into a £4,000 fundraiser for her friend
item.description: Empowered by compassion, five-year-old Rosie is taking on a four-mile scooter challenge in a princess dress to support her friend Sid's home adaptations. Incredibly, she has raised more than four thousand pounds to help Sid obtain necessary modifications, including a through-floor lift and accessible facilities. Sid's family expresses deep gratitude for Rosie's inspiring initiative and unwavering generosity during this crucial time.

item.title: Mexico cleaned 100K+ tons of sargassum in 2026, but the seaweed crisis is now threatening its tourism
item.description: In 2026, a massive expanse of Sargassum seaweed has taken over the Atlantic Ocean, wreaking havoc on coastal areas. Mexico is facing an unprecedented surge in seaweed accumulation, which is damaging its tourism sector. The foul odor has led to a notable decline in visitors, leaving local businesses in distress. Though scientists predict improvement by late autumn, a permanent solution is still unknown.

item.title: Taiwan researchers engineer interface only 0.42 nm thick to improve next-gen MoS2 transistors
item.description: Researchers from National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and TSMC have developed a new interface design for atomically thin transistors. They created a 0.42-nanometre aluminium oxide layer between monolayer MoS2 and a hafnium oxide dielectric. The design helped the transistors maintain strong electrical control and carrier transport while using an extremely thin insulating layer.

item.title: Why US is questioning Pakistan's Rs 3 trillion defence spending
item.description: The US State Department has flagged Pakistan's limited oversight of military and intelligence spending. Concerns were also raised regarding government debt disclosure and budget proposal publication delays. Pakistan's defence allocation has significantly increased for the upcoming financial year. The report urges greater transparency in military and intelligence budgets. This assessment highlights ongoing fiscal transparency challenges for Pakistan.

item.title: Russia kills 10 in Ukraine as Zelenskyy accuses Moscow of using N Korean missiles
item.description: Russian missile and drone attacks killed at least ten civilians across Ukraine on Tuesday. President Zelenskyy accused Moscow of using North Korean ballistic missiles in strikes. Ukraine warned Russia is exploiting its air defense interceptor shortages. Meanwhile, Ukraine struck Russian oil facilities, causing damage and casualties. The conflict continues with both sides expanding long-range strike capabilities.
